title: Infra GPU capacity, Terraform modules, and CI/CD runbook
author: Priya Menon
body:
Summary:
This runbook documents the operational patterns, Terraform/IaC modules, CI/CD build pipeline, networking and cloud account considerations, and runbook procedures for Redwood's GPU fleet and capacity management. It is intended for infra engineers, oncall SREs, and platform owners responsible for maintaining predictable capacity for model serving.

Scope and audience:
- Scope: GPU fleet provisioning (cloud accounts, VPC/networking), Terraform modules (reusable patterns), CI/CD for infra modules and fleet images, capacity autoscaling policies, and runbook procedures for common incidents.
- Audience: infra engineers, platform SREs, release engineers, and solutions engineers supporting Dedicated/private deployments.

High-level architecture overview:
- GPU fleet is organized by region -> cloud account -> pool (instance type + quant/sku).
- Terraform modules are used for: network (vpc, subnets, routing), iam and service principals, gpu-pool (instance profiles, autoscaling group / node pool), bastion and image build, and monitoring (prometheus + metrics exporters).
- CI/CD: GitHub Actions triggers for module lint/test/plan/apply; image build pipeline published to internal registry; module release uses semantic version tags and module registry.

Ownership and contacts:
- Primary owner: infra-gpu (team slack: #infra-gpu, pager: infra-gpu-oncall).
- Secondary owner: cloud-accounts (team slack: #cloud-accounts).
- Oncall rotation: infra-platform-oncall (see /confluence/eng-sre/slo-and-error-budgets for paging rules).

Terraform/IaC module catalog (recommended set):
1) module/networking-vpc - Creates VPC, public/private subnets, NAT gateways, route tables.
2) module/iam-service-roles - Centralized IAM roles and instance profiles for serving runtime.
3) module/gpu-pool - Creates node pools / autoscaling groups, attaches instance profiles, configures spot vs reserved mix.
4) module/image-builder - AMI/VM image pipeline integration with Packer and signing.
5) module/monitoring-exporters - Installs GPU exporter and sidecar metrics forwarders.
6) module/bastion-and-ssh - Secure access controls, session manager integration.

Module usage patterns and example (YAML/manifest):
- Keep modules small and composable. Each module must accept tags, owner, region, and cluster identifiers.
- Enforce remote state: use an `s3` (or cloud equivalent) backend with state locking.

Example snippet (illustrative):
```
module "gpu_pool_main" {
  source        = "github.com/redwood-inference/infra-modules//gpu-pool"
  region        = "us-west-2"
  instance_type = "p4d.24xlarge"
  min_size      = 2
  max_size      = 40
  subnets       = module.networking-vpc.private_subnets
  spot_percentage = 50
  tags = {
    Owner = "infra-gpu"
    Environment = "prod"
  }
}
```

CI/CD and build pipeline (conventions):
- Branching: repo-per-module with protected `main`. All changes require pull requests and at least 1 approver from infra-gov.
- CI checks: `terraform fmt`, `tflint`, `terraform init -backend=false`, `terraform plan` (with plan output artifact), unit tests (terratest where applicable), and security scanning (checkov / tfsec).
- Plan artifact: store JSON plan artifacts in S3 for auditability and automated drift detection.
- Apply: `apply` only from CI when PRs are merged, gated by a `terraform-apply` pipeline that requires a manual approval for production workspaces.
- Image builds: Packer -> image pipeline builds AMIs/VM images in a build account. Images are signed and promoted through dev->staging->prod registries.

Autoscaling and capacity policies:
- Preferred policy: target-tracking autoscaler based on GPU utilization and queue length metrics.
- Emergency burst policy: allow +20% temporary headroom using reserved on-demand instances for 15 minutes to absorb sudden spikes.
- Spot fallback: keep a base of on-demand capacity for critical services (recommended min 20% on-demand for prod).
- Pre-warm strategy: scheduled scaling for predictable traffic (weekly model release windows).

Networking and cloud accounts guidance:
- Cloud accounts per environment: prod, staging, dev, build (image), logging (centralized).
- VPC design: separate control plane subnets and data-plane private subnets. Ensure proper NACLs and flow logs enabled.
- Security groups: restrict serving nodes to only necessary egress for model downloads and registry; management plane ports limited to bastion and SSM.
- Cross-account access: use IAM roles with least privilege and short-lived credentials; centralize audit logs with an ingestion account.

Monitoring, alerts, and SLOs (recommended thresholds):
- Metrics to collect: GPU_utilization_95, GPU_memory_free_pct, Pod_restart_rate, Provision_time_95 (time from scale-up to ready), Queue_length.
- Alerts:
  - P1 (pager): Provision_time_95 > 10m AND Queue_length > 200 (sustained 5m).
  - P1: GPU_utilization_95 > 95% (sustained 5m) with no recent scale-up events.
  - P2 (channel): GPU_memory_free_pct < 15% on >10% of nodes.
  - P2: Terraform apply failed in prod pipeline.
- SLOs: 99.95% pod readiness for serving-critical pools; median provision_time < 90s.

Runbook: common incidents and playbooks:
1) Incident: Capacity shortage (high queue and long provision time)
   - Symptoms: Queue_length rising, provision_time_95 > 5m, requests timing out.
   - Immediate actions:
     1. Page infra-gpu oncall.
     2. Check autoscaler logs and recent scaling events (Grafana -> autoscaler dashboard).
     3. If autoscaler failing to scale: run `kubectl describe hpa` / check cloud API quotas.
     4. Apply emergency scale (manual increase) in the cloud console only when safe: increase pool desired to +30% (record change in incident log).
     5. If cloud quota hit: open cloud support ticket and switch traffic to fallback region or lower-tier model variant policy.
   - Postmortem actions: increase headroom, tune target metrics, and run capacity game-day.

2) Incident: Node boot failures / image regression
   - Symptoms: New instances failing health checks, failing to join cluster, or driver failures on GPU init.
   - Immediate actions:
     1. Revert to previous signed image in the image registry and re-provision a small batch.
     2. Inspect instance system logs (cloud console or `journalctl`) for driver/kmod errors.
     3. If a kernel/driver mismatch: stop deployment and notify image owners.
   - Postmortem actions: enforce stronger image canary (small rolling updates) and automated smoke tests for GPU drivers.

3) Incident: Networking connectivity between control plane and nodes
   - Symptoms: Nodes not contacting control plane, remote exec failing, metrics missing.
   - Immediate actions:
     1. Verify routing tables, NACLs and VPC peering status.
     2. Check flow logs for dropped traffic.
     3. If route table misconfiguration detected: apply corrective Terraform change in dev, promote with short approval window for prod.

Operational processes and checklists:
- Weekly: capacity health check (utilization by pool, pending jobs, spot eviction rate).
- Monthly: run scaling game-day, validate disaster recovery (DR) plan for region failover, test image rollback.
- Quarterly: review cloud account quotas and reservations, evaluate instance family upgrades, and update cost projections.

CI/CD run examples and commands:
- Local plan reproduction: `terraform init && terraform plan -out=plan.tfplan && terraform show -json plan.tfplan > plan.json`
- Run acceptance tests: `go test ./test/ -run TestGpuPoolProvisioning` (terratest harness).
- Promote image: pipeline creates signed tag `ami-2026-03-01-prod-1.2.3` and publishes to prod registry after manual approval.

Deployment and release notes checklist (for infra changes impacting prod):
- Change summary and risk classification.
- Rollback plan and previous image/TF state.
- Preflight checks (quota, health checks, smoke tests).
- One-hour maintenance window if required.

Troubleshooting quick commands:
- Check autoscaler status: `kubectl get hpa -n serving`
- Check node GPU driver: `ssh node && nvidia-smi`
- Inspect instance limits: cloud CLI `aws ec2 describe-instance-limits --region us-west-2`
- Retrieve terraform plan artifact: `aws s3 cp s3://tfplans/prod/gpu_pool/plan-<id>.json .`

Templates and examples included in repo:
- smoke-tests/ (image smoke tests for driver + runtime)
- terraform/modules/gpu-pool/examples/ (prod and staging example configs)
- ci/pipelines/terraform-apply.yml (protected prod apply pipeline)

Related pages and references:
- Infra GPU guide: /confluence/eng-infra/terraform-and-iac/infra-iac-and-gpu-fleet-guide-2026
- GPU runbook: /confluence/eng-infra/runbooks/gpu-capacity-and-infra-runbook-2026
- SRE SLOs: /confluence/eng-sre/slo-and-error-budgets

Appendix: decision history and rationales:
- We prefer a small on-demand baseline (>=20%) to avoid serving disruption from spot evictions.
- Use signed images to prevent accidental rollout of untested kernel/driver combinations.
- Manual approvals are required for production Terraform applies to reduce blast radius.

Revision history:
- 2026-02-10: Created by Priya Menon.
- 2026-03-01: Updated CI/CD gating and example snippets (reviewers: Diego Alvarez, Meera Patel).

If you find gaps or want a deeper runbook for a specific cloud provider (AWS/GCP/Azure) or private on-prem packaging, file a request with infra-gpu and tag `operations-request`.
